apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-redis
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.redis.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
      app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
        app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: redis
          image: "redis:{{ .Values.redis.imageTag | default "7-alpine" }}"
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.global.imagePullPolicy | default "IfNotPresent" }}
          ports:
            - name: redis
              containerPort: 6379
              protocol: TCP
          livenessProbe:
            tcpSocket:
              port: 6379
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - redis-cli
                - ping
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
          resources:
            {{- toYaml .Values.redis.resources | nindent 12 }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-redis-service
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
spec:
  type: {{ .Values.redis.service.type | default "ClusterIP" }}
  ports:
    - port: 6379
      targetPort: 6379
      protocol: TCP
      name: redis
  selector:
    {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redis

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-redis
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.redis.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
      app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
        app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: redis
          image: "redis:{{ .Values.redis.imageTag | default "7-alpine" }}"
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.global.imagePullPolicy | default "IfNotPresent" }}
          ports:
            - name: redis
              containerPort: 6379
              protocol: TCP
          livenessProbe:
            tcpSocket:
              port: 6379
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - redis-cli
                - ping
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
          resources:
            {{- toYaml .Values.redis.resources | nindent 12 }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-redis-service
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redis
spec:
  type: {{ .Values.service.type | default "ClusterIP" }}
  ports:
    - port: 6379
      targetPort: 6379
      protocol: TCP
      name: redis
  selector:
    {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redis

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-frontend
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.frontend.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
      app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
        app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: frontend
          image: "{{ .Values.global.imageRegistry }}{{ if .Values.global.imageRegistry }}/{{ end }}frontend:{{ .Values.frontend.imageTag }}"
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.global.imagePullPolicy }}
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          resources:
            {{- toYaml .Values.frontend.resources | nindent 12 }}
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-frontend-service
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend
spec:
  selector:
    {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 3000
      targetPort: 3000
  type: {{ .Values.service.type | default "ClusterIP" }}

# Local deployment values for cue-platform Helm chart
# For deployment on a local k3s/minikube cluster

# Global image settings
global:
  imageRegistry: ""
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Backend services configuration
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  imageTag: latest
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Frontend configuration
frontend:
  imageTag: latest
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# PostgreSQL configuration
postgres:
  imageTag: 15-3.4
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 5Gi

# RabbitMQ configuration
rabbitmq:
  imageTag: "3-management"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Redis configuration
redis:
  imageTag: "7-alpine"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m
    requests:
      memory: 64Mi
      cpu: 50m

# Jaeger configuration (distributed tracing)
jaeger:
  imageTag: "1.47"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Secrets configuration - Plain text values (will be base64 encoded by Helm chart)
secret:
  # PostgreSQL credentials
  POSTGRES_USER: admin
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localsecret
  POSTGRES_DB: cue_db

  # RabbitMQ credentials
  RABBITMQ_USER: admin
  RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: localsecret

  # Redis password
  REDIS_PASSWORD: localsecret

  # Stripe API key for payments (use test key for local)
  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: sk_test_421ffVAem5k5Ea8 # placeholder

  # JWT signing key for authentication tokens
  JWT_SIGNING_KEY: supersecretjwtskieforlocalhev

  # Auth Service specific secrets
  JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES: "15" # Access token expiry in minutes
  JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS: "7" # Refresh token expiry in days

  # Database connection strings (will be generated from postgres service)
  AUTH_DB_CONNECTION: Host=cue-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=admin;Password=localsecret
  USER_DB_CONNECTION: Host=cue-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue;Username=admin;Password=localsecret
  BOOKING_DB_CONNECTION: Host=cue-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cues;Username=adm;Password=localsecret
  PAYMENT_DB_CONNECTION: Host=cue-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cues;Username=adm;Password=localsecret
  ConnectionStrings__CueDatabase: Host=cue-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=admin;Password=localsecret

  # Email service credentials
  EMAIL_API_KEY: local # placeholder
  EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS: cue@localhost.local

  # Redis connection strings
  REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING: redis://redis:6379

  # RabbitMQ connection
  RABBITMQ_CONNECTION_STRING: amqp://admin:localsecret@rabbitmq:5672

  # Jaeger tracing endpoint
  JAEGER_AGENT_HOST: jaeger-agent-split-jeager:6831

# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci

# Copy source
COPY . .

# Build the app
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:20-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Install a lightweight HTTP server to serve the static build
RUN npm install -g serve

# Copy built artifacts from builder
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000', (r) => {if (r.statusCode !== 200) throw new Error(r.statusCode)})"

# Start the application
CMD ["serve", "-s", "dist", "-l", "3000"]

input.content:
# Plan: Implement Ingress for Frontend and API Gateway

## Context
The user wants to expose the frontend via Ingress and have it reverse proxy to the API Gateway, which then routes traffic to backend services (already implemented via Ocelot).

Currently:
- Frontend is deployed as a Deployment + Service (ClusterIP on port 3000)
- API Gateway is deployed as a Deployment + Service (ClusterIP on port 8080)
- Backend services are deployed as Deployments + Services (ClusterIP on port 8080)
- Ingress is configured in `values.yaml` but no Ingress template exists

## Architecture
```
External Traffic → Ingress (nginx) → / → Frontend (port 3000)
                                    → /api/* → API Gateway (port 8080) → Backend Services (Ocelot routes)
```

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Create Ingress Template (`helm-chart/templates/ingress.yaml`)
Create a new Ingress resource that:
- Routes `/` path to `{{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-frontend-service` on port 3000
- Routes `/api` path to `api-gateway` on port 8080
- Uses configurable annotations, className, and TLS from `values.yaml`
- Supports multiple hosts from `values.yaml`

### 2. Update Frontend to Proxy API Calls
The frontend (served by `serve`) needs to proxy `/api` calls to the API Gateway. Options:
- **Option A**: Configure nginx as a sidecar in the frontend pod (more complex)
- **Option B**: Use Ingress path-based routing (simpler, recommended)

Since the Ingress handles path-based routing, the frontend just needs to make API calls to `/api/...` and the Ingress will route them to the API Gateway.

### 3. Update API Gateway Ocelot Configuration
The Ocelot config uses upstream paths like `/api/v1/auth/{everything}` and `/api/auth/{everything}`. The Ingress should strip the `/api` prefix or the Ocelot config needs to match. Currently Ocelot expects both `/api/v1/...` and `/api/...` paths, which matches what the Ingress will forward.

### 4. Update Values Files
- Ensure `values.yaml` and `values-local.yaml` have appropriate Ingress configuration (host, TLS, annotations)
- For local development, add a host like `cue.local` and configure `/etc/hosts`

## Files to Modify/Create

1. **Create**: `helm-chart/templates/ingress.yaml` - New Ingress template
2. **Review**: `helm-chart/values.yaml` - Ensure Ingress config is appropriate
3. **Review**: `helm-chart/values-local.yaml` - Add local Ingress config (host, TLS if needed)

## Ingress Template Design

```yaml
{{- if .Values.ingress.enabled }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-ingress
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  {{- with .Values.ingress.annotations }}
  annotations:
    {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
  {{- end }}
spec:
  {{- if .Values.ingress.className }}
  ingressClassName: {{ .Values.ingress.className }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ingress.tls }}
  tls:
    {{- toYaml .Values.ingress.tls | nindent 4 }}
  {{- end }}
  rules:
    {{- range .Values.ingress.hosts }}
    - host: {{ .host | quote }}
      http:
        paths:
          {{- range .paths }}
          - path: {{ .path }}
            pathType: {{ .pathType }}
            backend:
              service:
                name: {{ include "cue.fullname" $ }}-frontend-service
                port:
                  number: 3000
          {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

## Verification Steps

1. Deploy with `helm upgrade cue ./helm-chart -n cue-platform -f ./helm-chart/values-local.yaml --create-namespace`
2. Check Ingress is created: `kubectl get ingress -n cue-platform`
3. Verify frontend accessible at configured host
4. Verify API calls to `/api/...` reach API Gateway
5. Test end-to-end: frontend → API Gateway → backend services

## Questions for User

1. What hostname should be used for local development? (e.g., `cue.local`, `localhost`, etc.)
2. Should we use nginx-ingress controller or another ingress controller?
3. Do you want TLS/HTTPS for local development (self-signed certs)?
4. Should the frontend make API calls to `/api/...` (relative paths) or to an absolute URL?

# Plan: Implement Ingress for Frontend and API Gateway

## Context
The user wants to expose the frontend via Ingress and have it reverse proxy to the API Gateway, which then routes traffic to backend services (already implemented via Ocelot).

Currently:
- Frontend is deployed as a Deployment + Service (ClusterIP on port 3000)
- API Gateway is deployed as a Deployment + Service (ClusterIP on port 8080)
- Backend services are deployed as Deployments + Services (ClusterIP on port 8080)
- Ingress is configured in `values.yaml` but no Ingress template exists

## Architecture
```
External Traffic → Ingress (nginx) → / → Frontend (port 3000)
                                    → /api/* → API Gateway (port 8080) → Backend Services (Ocelot routes)
```

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Create Ingress Template (`helm-chart/templates/ingress.yaml`)
Create a new Ingress resource that:
- Routes `/` path to `{{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-frontend-service` on port 3000
- Routes `/api` path to `api-gateway` on port 8080
- Uses configurable annotations, className, and TLS from `values.yaml`
- Supports multiple hosts from `values.yaml`

### 2. Update Frontend to Proxy API Calls
The frontend (served by `serve`) needs to proxy `/api` calls to the API Gateway. Options:
- **Option A**: Configure nginx as a sidecar in the frontend pod (more complex)
- **Option B**: Use Ingress path-based routing (simpler, recommended)

Since the Ingress handles path-based routing, the frontend just needs to make API calls to `/api/...` and the Ingress will route them to the API Gateway.

### 3. Update API Gateway Ocelot Configuration
The Ocelot config uses upstream paths like `/api/v1/auth/{everything}` and `/api/auth/{everything}`. The Ingress should strip the `/api` prefix or the Ocelot config needs to match. Currently Ocelot expects both `/api/v1/...` and `/api/...` paths, which matches what the Ingress will forward.

### 4. Update Values Files
- Ensure `values.yaml` and `values-local.yaml` have appropriate Ingress configuration (host, TLS, annotations)
- For local development, add a host like `cue.local` and configure `/etc/hosts`

## Files to Modify/Create

1. **Create**: `helm-chart/templates/ingress.yaml` - New Ingress template
2. **Review**: `helm-chart/values.yaml` - Ensure Ingress config is appropriate
3. **Review**: `helm-chart/values-local.yaml` - Add local Ingress config (host, TLS if needed)

## Ingress Template Design

```yaml
{{- if .Values.ingress.enabled }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-ingress
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  {{- with .Values.ingress.annotations }}
  annotations:
    {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
  {{- end }}
spec:
  {{- if .Values.ingress.className }}
  ingressClassName: {{ .Values.ingress.className }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ingress.tls }}
  tls:
    {{- toYaml .Values.ingress.tls | nindent 4 }}
  {{- end }}
  rules:
    {{- range .Values.ingress.hosts }}
    - host: {{ .host | quote }}
      http:
        paths:
          {{- range .paths }}
          - path: {{ .path }}
            pathType: {{ .pathType }}
            backend:
              service:
                name: {{ include "cue.fullname" $ }}-frontend-service
                port:
                  number: 3000
          {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

## Verification Steps

1. Deploy with `helm upgrade cue ./helm-chart -n cue-platform -f ./helm-chart/values-local.yaml --create-namespace`
2. Check Ingress is created: `kubectl get ingress -n cue-platform`
3. Verify frontend accessible at configured host
4. Verify API calls to `/api/...` reach API Gateway
5. Test end-to-end: frontend → API Gateway → backend services

## Questions for User

1. What hostname should be used for local development? (e.g., `cue.local`, `localhost`, etc.)
2. Should we use nginx-ingress controller or another ingress controller?
3. Do you want TLS/HTTPS for local development (self-signed certs)?
4. Should the frontend make API calls to `/api/...` (relative paths) or to an absolute URL?
